pass_a_gloss: But let us hear of the Lord recounting and saying: 'If I cannot do to you as the potter does, O house of Israel?' says the Lord. Behold, as the clay of the potter, so you are in my hand. I will speak against a nation and kingdom to pluck up and destroy; and that nation will turn back from the evil of which I spoke against it, and I will relent concerning the evil I thought to do to them. Again I will speak against a nation and kingdom to build and plant; and they will do evil before me, not listening to my voice, and I will relent concerning the good I spoke to do for them,' says the Lord. We see this according to the potter's house being recalled not upon one of each, but upon two nations; for he begins saying that he is about to speak concerning nations, so that he may subtly suggest to those able to hear hidden mysteries: 'I will speak against a nation. Seek also the end and the former nation, from which he speaks of destruction due to their sins; and having spoken of destruction due to their sins, he still promises that if they repent, he will relent concerning the evil of which he spoke to do to them. And again he speaks concerning another nation, the second, 'to be built and to be planted,' a whole nation; and since this built and planted nation has a good promise, yet can sin, he says after speaking these things: if they withdraw from good works, 'I will relent concerning the good things I spoke to do for them.' What then are the two nations, the former named which the word threatens, and the latter which it promises? It threatens thus, that if they repent, I will not do the things of the threat. It promises thus, that if they turn aside and it becomes unworthy that the second nation of the promises should not obtain them. Especially concerning two nations is all the economy of God set before men in the world. First became that nation Israel, second from the Christ's advent this nation. To the former God threatened what he threatened, and we see the things of the threat of the former nation: they have become captive, their city destroyed, the sanctuary demolished, the altar thrown down, nothing remains of the ancient venerable things among them. For God said to that nation: 'Repent, and they did not repent.' After these things were spoken to them, he says to this second nation the things concerning its being built. He sees also that this nation consists of men able again to fall away. Therefore he also threatens it and says: 'Even if I foretold the things concerning building, planting, and agriculture, yet it is about to sin, this nation, and if it sins, the same things will happen to it as were said to those because of their sins, and they will suffer if they do not repent.' Search all the scripture, and you will find most things concerning these two nations spoken. God chose the fathers, gave them a promise, brought forth a people from the lineage of the fathers from Egypt, was long-suffering toward them sinning, instructed them as a father, brought them in, gave them the land of promise, sent prophets to them in due season, instructed and turned them back from their sins. He was long-suffering continually sending the healers until the chief physician should come. The differing one among prophets is a prophet, the differing one among physicians is a physician. Having come, this one they forwarded and killed, saying 'Take away, take away,' saying 'From the earth take away such a one,' 'cross, cross him.' Immediately there came an inspection upon the nation, the place was made desolate where my Jesus was crucified, God chose another nation. The harvest you see how great it is, even if the workers are few. And otherwise God always orders the net to be cast into the sea of this life and gathered are fish of every kind; he sends out 'the many fishermen,' he sends out 'the many hunters,' they hunt from 'every mountain,' they hunt from 'every hill.' See how great the economy is concerning the salvation of the nations. 'See therefore the goodness and severity of God: upon indeed the former nation having fallen, severity; but upon you the second nation, promises and 'goodness, if you remain in goodness'; since and you will be cut off. For not the axe, but only then was it laid against the root of the trees. Again ready is the axe to come: 'the' 'axe lies against the root of the trees' Jesus said to me then prophesying concerning Israel beside which the axe was. He himself was the axe of the barren tree and said: 'Already the axe lies against the root of the trees. All that were there trees not producing fruit were cut off and cast into the fire and burned. But now another cultivation has come about analogous to the former, concerning which it was said: 'Having brought in, plant them into the mountain of your inheritance, into a ready dwelling place of yours.' God brought their nation into the mountain of his inheritance. The mountain I seek not as Jews do in insensible matter. The mountain is Christ. In this we were planted, in him we were guarded. See therefore, if even he should be long-suffering, lest coming the householder should say: 'Already three years I come upon this fig tree and it has not borne fruit; cut it down; why then also the ground be left idle?' For it leaves idle the good ground, Christ, the mystery of the church, the one coming upon the synagogue and not bearing fruit.
